title: Hall of Fantasy
paragraphs: A supernatural anthology of eerie fantasy and horror stories, especially associated with writer-producer Richard Thorne.
Supernatural, fantasy and horror anthology associated with Richard Thorne.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: KALL local incarnation (1946 to May 4, 1947) on [[org|org.530c043ded979268|KALL]], WGN Chicago local revival (1949 to August 21, 1952) on [[org|org.06b4214104618161|WGN]], Mutual network run (August 22, 1952 to September 28, 1953) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Later rebroadcast/syndication cycle (October 5, 1953 to March 29, 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Richard Thorne (writer, performer, and producer), Harold Turner (music and organist), Leroy Olliger (director), Carl Grayson (performer), Harry Elders (performer), Jim Ameche (performer), and Wayne Dickenson (sound-effects artist).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.06b4214104618161|WGN]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to death, murder and lethal danger, supernatural forces, ghosts and the uncanny, curses, haunted objects and supernatural revenge, classic supernatural and horror literature, occult ritual, idols and dark magic, and monsters, creatures and nonhuman threats.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Regional local-radio anthology development, National Mutual supernatural anthology, Classic supernatural literature on radio, and Post-network rebroadcast and syndication cycle.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|gang-busters|Gang Busters]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|suspense|Suspense]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]].
